title: dedicated-autoscaler: improve burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: Customers on Dedicated capacity observed degraded tail latency and cost spikes when temporary traffic bursts exhausted token-bucket burst allowances and triggered aggressive scale-ups. This PR introduces smoother burst controls, clearer throughput guarantee semantics, and richer utilization reporting to help operators tune policies. High level changes: 1) TokenBucket smoothing: add exponential decay on available burst tokens to avoid instantaneous large drains and to allow graceful shedding under sustained pressure. 2) Throughput guarantees: introduce explicit per-fleet throughput floor and soft-guarantee path that prefers queuing with backpressure instead of immediate instance allocation for short bursts. 3) Burst controls policy refactor: unify burst args into a single policy object (burst_capacity, refill_rate, smoothing_factor, max_burst_window) with validation and runtime defaults. 4) Utilization reporting: emit per-fleet, per-priority utilization histograms (p50/p95/p99) and a derived "burst_consumption" metric to correlate burst usage with scale events. 5) Observability: add logs and tracing spans for token-bucket state transitions and scale decision reasons. Backwards compatibility: old policy fields are supported via a migration layer and will log deprecation warnings. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-3452) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] metrics dashboards updated - [x] canary rollout plan - [x] docs and release notes Changes include code path refactors and new metrics; no API surface breaking changes expected. Rollout: feature gate behind rollout.platform.dedicated_autoscaler_v2; canary on 5% of fleets for 48 hours with nightly utilization reports; auto-rollback on error rate increase >2x baseline or median 99th percentile latency regression >15%. Related: references ENG-3452 and previous autotune work in ENG-3201. For support-bug SUP-789 this change reduces incident frequency by preventing noisy scaling churn. Testing: unit tests for tokenbucket logic cover edge cases (zero refill, burst undershoot/overshoot), integration tests simulate synthetic burst patterns and assert expected backpressure vs scale decision, e2e on staging confirmed 12% median cost reduction and 22% fewer scale events for 10s-30s bursts. Documentation: console docs updated to show new burst policy knobs and recommended defaults.

release_notes: Improved Dedicated autoscaler: smoother burst handling, explicit throughput guarantees, and enhanced utilization metrics. Changes are behind a feature flag and include migration support for legacy policy fields. Expected benefits: reduced noisy scale events and improved cost stability during short bursts.
canary_plan: Canary 5% fleets for 48 hours, monitor error rate and p99 latency, nightly utilization report. Auto-rollback on >2x error rate or >15% p99 latency regression.
